saints.name: St. Isidore of Seville
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The last of the Latin Fathers, whose learning gathered the wisdom of the ancient world for a new age…
biography: Born at Cartagena about 560 into a family that gave the Church four saints, Isidore succeeded his brother Leander as Archbishop of Seville around the year 600. He completed the conversion of the Visigoths of Spain from Arianism and presided over councils, chief among them the Fourth Council of Toledo in 633, which ordered a school in every diocese.

Isidore is best remembered as an encyclopaedist: his Etymologies gathered and preserved the learning of the ancient world for the medieval West, and his historical and theological works were read for centuries. Often called the last of the Latin Fathers, he died in 636 and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1722; because his great work sought to organize all knowledge, he is popularly proposed as a patron of students and the Internet.
saints.knownFor: His Etymologies and his labour to preserve ancient learning.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church (1722)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 4 April
